What happens if you never sleep?
In 1964, a seventeen-year-old named Randy Gardner tried to find out.
He stayed awake for eleven days straight.
By day two, he couldn't focus his eyes.
By day four, he was seeing things that weren't there.
He thought a street sign was a person.
By day eleven, he couldn't finish simple math.
He'd forget what he was saying, in the middle of a sentence.
After about eighteen hours awake, your reactions are as bad as someone who's been drinking.
And your brain starts taking microsleeps...
tiny naps, a few seconds long, without you noticing.
But record books stopped accepting attempts like his.
